candidates: When adding or updating branch-based Live Editor preview environments, use the `<branch>.git.mermaid.live` subdomain naming convention to unambiguously signal that the site is built from a git branch. Do not use names like `beta.mermaid.live` that could be confused with npm pre-release (beta/rc) publishes — the two deployment mechanisms are distinct and the name must reflect which one is in use.

In user-facing documentation (e.g., README, issue templates) that references branch-based preview environments, use wording that clearly conveys the content is an unreleased git-branch preview (e.g., 'git `develop` branch preview' or 'preview of future releases'). Avoid phrases such as 'latest version' or similar language that could imply official or stable-release status.

When `scripts/editor.bash` (or any equivalent branch-deploy build script) packages mermaid for a preview environment, append the short git commit hash to the mermaid package version (e.g., via `jq` on `packages/mermaid/package.json`) so that users of the preview site can immediately identify which commit it was built from and debug stale-deploy issues.
